141	        "conversations": [
142	            {
143	                "from": "human",
144	                "value": "<image>\nWhat's the main object in this picture?"
145	            },
146	            {
147	                "from": "gpt",
148	                "value": "A green orange on a plastic table"
149	            }
150	        ]
151	    }
152	]
153	```
154	
155	Some examples are shown in `demo/single_images.json` and `demo/video.json` and these json files could be used for training.
156	
157	### Dataset config for training
158	
159	To add or modify datasets for training, follow these steps:
160	
161	### Dataset Definition Structure
162	
163	1. **Create a dataset dictionary** in the format in the file `data/__init__.py`:
164	```python
165	DATASET_NAME = {
166	    "annotation_path": "/path/to/annotations.json",
167	    "data_path": "/path/to/image/data",  # Can be empty if paths are in annotations
168	}
169	```
170	
171	2. **Register your dataset** by adding it to the `data_dict`:
172	```python
173	data_dict = {
174	    "your_dataset_name": DATASET_NAME,
175	    # ... other datasets
176	}
177	```
178	
179	### Sampling Rate Control
180	
181	You can optionally specify sampling rates by appending `%X` to the dataset name:
182	- `"dataset_name%50"` will sample 50% of the data
183	- `"dataset_name%20"` will sample 20% of the data
184	
185	### Usage Example
186	
187	1. Define your dataset:
188	```python
189	MY_DATASET = {
190	    "annotation_path": "/data/my_dataset/annotations.json",
191	    "data_path": "/data/my_dataset/images/",
192	}
193	
194	data_dict = {
195	    "my_dataset": MY_DATASET,
196	    "cambrian_737k": CAMBRIAN_737K,  # existing dataset
197	}
198	```
199	
200	2. Use it in training:
201	```python
202	dataset_names = ["my_dataset%50"]  # Will use 50% of your dataset
203	configs = data_list(dataset_names)
204	```
205	
206	### Notes  
207	- The `annotation_path` should point to a JSON or JSONL file containing your dataset annotations.  
208	- The `data_path` can be left empty if the image paths in the annotations are absolute.  
209	- Sampling rates are applied per-dataset when multiple datasets are specified.  
210	- Some datasets you can use directly: `nyu-visionx/Cambrian-10M`, `lmms-lab/LLaVA-NeXT-Data`, `FreedomIntelligence/ALLaVA-4V`, `TIGER-Lab/VisualWebInstruct`.  
211	- The training data should strictly follow this format:  
212	  - One `<image>` tag in the question must correspond to exactly one image file  
213	  - Similarly, `<video>` tags must correspond to video files  
214	  - These special tokens should not appear in the answer text  
215	- For open source data that might have missing images or other issues, you can verify data completeness using `tools/check_image.py`.  
216	
217	
218	## Usage
219	
220	To train a model:
221	
222	```bash
223	#!/bin/bash
224	# Complete QwenVL Training Launch Script with Full Parameter Documentation
225	
226	# ======================
227	# Distributed Configuration
228	# ======================
229	MASTER_ADDR="127.0.0.1"                     # [Required] Master node IP for multi-GPU training
230	MASTER_PORT=$(shuf -i 20000-29999 -n 1)     # Random port to avoid conflicts
231	NPROC_PER_NODE=$(nvidia-smi --list-gpus | wc -l)  # Automatically detects available GPUs
232	
233	# ======================
234	# Path Configuration
235	# ======================
236	MODEL_PATH="/path/to/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct"  # [ModelArguments] Pretrained model path
237	OUTPUT_DIR="./checkpoints"                   # Directory for saving checkpoints
238	CACHE_DIR="./cache"                          # [TrainingArguments] Cache directory for models
239	
240	# ======================
241	# Model Configuration
242	# ======================
243	DATASETS="your_dataset%100"                  # [DataArguments] Dataset with sampling rate
244	
245	# ======================
246	# Training Hyperparameters
247	# ======================
248	torchrun --nproc_per_node=$NPROC_PER_NODE \
249	         --master_addr=$MASTER_ADDR \
250	         --master_port=$MASTER_PORT \
251	         qwenvl/train/train_qwen.py \
252	         # Core Arguments
253	         --model_name_or_path $MODEL_PATH \  # [ModelArguments] Model identifier
254	         --tune_mm_llm True \                # [TrainingArguments] Train LLM or not
255	         --tune_mm_vision False \            # [TrainingArguments] Train VIT or not
256	         --tune_mm_mlp False \               # [TrainingArguments] Train MLP or not
257	         --dataset_use $DATASETS \           # [DataArguments] Dataset specification
258	         --output_dir $OUTPUT_DIR \          # Output directory for checkpoints
259	         --cache_dir $CACHE_DIR \            # [TrainingArguments] Model cache location
260	         
261	         # Precision & Memory
262	         --bf16 \                            # Use bfloat16 precision (Ampere+ GPUs)
263	         --per_device_train_batch_size 4 \   # Batch size per GPU
264	         --gradient_accumulation_steps 4 \   # Effective batch size multiplier
265	         
266	         # Learning Rate Configuration
267	         --learning_rate 2e-7 \              # Base learning rate
268	         --mm_projector_lr 1e-5 \            # [TrainingArguments] Projector-specific LR
269	         --vision_tower_lr 1e-6 \            # [TrainingArguments] Vision encoder LR
270	         --optim adamw_torch \               # [TrainingArguments] Optimizer selection
271	         
272	         # Sequence Configuration
273	         --model_max_length 4096 \           # [TrainingArguments] Max sequence length
274	         --data_flatten True \               # [DataArguments] Concatenate batch sequences
275	         --data_packing True \               # [DataArguments] Using packing data
276	         
277	         # Image Processing
278	         --max_pixels 576\*28\*28 \               # [DataArguments] Max image pixels (H*W) for image
279	         --min_pixels 16\*28\*28 \                # [DataArguments] Min image pixels for image
280	         # Video Processing
281	         --video_fps 2 \                          # [DataArguments] video fps
282	         --video_max_frames 8 \                   # [DataArguments] Max frames per video
283	         --video_min_frames 4 \                   # [DataArguments] Min frames per video
284	         --video_max_pixels 1664\*28\*28 \        # [DataArguments] Max pixels per video
285	         --video_min_pixels 256\*28\*28 \         # [DataArguments] Min pixels per video
286	         
287	         # Training Schedule
288	         --num_train_epochs 3 \              # Total training epochs
289	         --warmup_ratio 0.03 \               # LR warmup proportion
290	         --lr_scheduler_type "cosine" \      # Learning rate schedule
291	         --weight_decay 0.01 \               # L2 regularization strength
292	         
293	         # Logging & Checkpoints
294	         --logging_steps 10 \               # Log metrics interval
295	         --save_steps 500 \                 # Checkpoint save interval
296	         --save_total_limit 3 \             # Max checkpoints to keep
297	
298	         # Lora Config
299	         --lora_enable True \                 # [TrainingArguments] Enable LoRA
300	         --lora_r 8 \                         # [TrainingArguments] LoRA r
301	         --lora_alpha 16 \                    # [TrainingArguments] LoRA alpha 
302	         --lora_dropout 0.0 \                # [TrainingArguments] LoRA dropout
303	
304	         # Advanced Options
305	         --deepspeed zero3.json \           # DeepSpeed configuration
306	```
307	
308	The script accepts arguments in three categories:
309	
310	   - Flags to control which components to tune (`tune_mm_vision`, `tune_mm_mlp`, `tune_mm_llm`). If trained with both image and video data, tune_mm_vision should be False: `tune_mm_vision=False`
311	   - `data_flatten` flag means data in a batch are concat into one sequence
312	   - `data_packing` requires preprocess with `tools/pack_data.py`
313	   - Training hyperparameters, the suggested learning rate is from 1e-6 to 2e-7
314	   - Training resolution is critical for the model performances, hence `--max_pixels` and `--min_pixels` should be properly set
315	   - Training with Qwen2.5-VL-32B model, you should have 8 80G GPU refering to `scripts/sft_32b.sh`
316	   - `"_attn_implementation": "flash_attention_2",` could be add in the config.json of the model to use flash attention.
317	   - The Qwen3VL MoE model does not support DeepSpeed with ZeRO-3. Additionally, Hugging Face’s official implementation does not include support for load balancing loss currently.
318

The `qwenvl` directory contains the following components:

### `train/`
- `trainer.py`: Main trainer updated from Huggingface Trainer
- `train_qwen.py`: Main file for training
- `argument.py`: Dataclasses for model, data and training arguments

### `data/`
- `__init__.py`: Contains datasets configs
- `data_processor.py`: Data processing module for QwenVL models
- `rope2d.py`: Provide RoPE implementation

### `tools`
- `process_bbox.ipynb`: Convert bbox into QwenVL format. If you have grounding data, please refer this file to tranform your data.
- `pack_data.py`: Pack data into even length buckets.

## Requirements

You could use follow version of packages:

- `torch==2.6.0`
- `torchvision==0.21.0`
- `transformers==4.57.0.dev0`
- `deepspeed==0.17.1`
- `flash_attn==2.7.4.post1`
- `triton==3.2.0`
- `accelerate==1.7.0`
- `torchcodec==0.2`
- `peft==0.17.1`

## Custom Dataset Configuration

The customized data should have the format like:

### JSON Data Structure

**Media Specification**:
- `image/video`: Contains path to the media file (required)
- Media tags in prompts:
    - `<image>` for image understanding tasks
    - `<video>` for video understanding tasks
- `conversations`: contains the questions and answers

### Example Instances:

1. **Single Image Example**:
```json
{
    "image": "images/001.jpg",
    "conversations": [
        {
            "from": "human",
            "value": "<image>\nWhat's the main object in this picture?"
        },
        {
            "from": "gpt",
            "value": "A red apple on a wooden table"
        }
    ]
}
```

2. **Multi-Image Example**:
```json
{
    "image": ["cats/001.jpg", "cats/002.jpg"],
    "conversations": [
        {
            "from": "human",
            "value": "<image>\n<image>\nWhat are the differences between these two cats?"
        },
        {
            "from": "gpt",
            "value": "The first cat is an orange tabby with short fur and green eyes, while the second is a gray Siamese with blue eyes and pointed coloration. They also appear to be in different environments - the first is indoors on a couch, the second is outdoors in a garden."

    ]
}
```

3. **Video Example**:
```json
{
    "video": "videos/005.mp4",
    "conversations": [
```

### Dataset config for training

To add or modify datasets for training, follow these steps:

### Dataset Definition Structure

1. **Create a dataset dictionary** in the format in the file `data/__init__.py`:
```python
DATASET_NAME = {
    "annotation_path": "/path/to/annotations.json",
    "data_path": "/path/to/image/data",  # Can be empty if paths are in annotations
}
```

2. **Register your dataset** by adding it to the `data_dict`:
```python
data_dict = {
    "your_dataset_name": DATASET_NAME,
    # ... other datasets
}
```

### Sampling Rate Control

You can optionally specify sampling rates by appending `%X` to the dataset name:
- `"dataset_name%50"` will sample 50% of the data
- `"dataset_name%20"` will sample 20% of the data

### Usage Example

1. Define your dataset:
```python
MY_DATASET = {
    "annotation_path": "/data/my_dataset/annotations.json",
    "data_path": "/data/my_dataset/images/",
}

data_dict = {
    "my_dataset": MY_DATASET,
    "cambrian_737k": CAMBRIAN_737K,  # existing dataset
}
```

2. Use it in training:
```python
dataset_names = ["my_dataset%50"]  # Will use 50% of your dataset
configs = data_list(dataset_names)
```

### Notes  
- The `annotation_path` should point to a JSON or JSONL file containing your dataset annotations.  
- The `data_path` can be left empty if the image paths in the annotations are absolute.  
- Sampling rates are applied per-dataset when multiple datasets are specified.  
- Some datasets you can use directly: `nyu-visionx/Cambrian-10M`, `lmms-lab/LLaVA-NeXT-Data`, `FreedomIntelligence/ALLaVA-4V`, `TIGER-Lab/VisualWebInstruct`.  
- The training data should strictly follow this format:  
  - One `<image>` tag in the question must correspond to exactly one image file  
  - Similarly, `<video>` tags must correspond to video files  
  - These special tokens should not appear in the answer text  
- For open source data that might have missing images or other issues, you can verify data completeness using `tools/check_image.py`.  


## Usage

To train a model:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Complete QwenVL Training Launch Script with Full Parameter Documentation

# ======================
# Distributed Configuration
# ======================
MASTER_ADDR="127.0.0.1"                     # [Required] Master node IP for multi-GPU training
MASTER_PORT=$(shuf -i 20000-29999 -n 1)     # Random port to avoid conflicts
NPROC_PER_NODE=$(nvidia-smi --list-gpus | wc -l)  # Automatically detects available GPUs

# ======================
# Path Configuration
# ======================
MODEL_PATH="/path/to/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct"  # [ModelArguments] Pretrained model path
OUTPUT_DIR="./checkpoints"                   # Directory for saving checkpoints
CACHE_DIR="./cache"                          # [TrainingArguments] Cache directory for models

# ======================
# Model Configuration
# ======================
DATASETS="your_dataset%100"                  # [DataArguments] Dataset with sampling rate

# ======================
# Training Hyperparameters
# ======================
torchrun --nproc_per_node=$NPROC_PER_NODE \
         --master_addr=$MASTER_ADDR \
         --master_port=$MASTER_PORT \
         qwenvl/train/train_qwen.py \
         # Core Arguments
         --model_name_or_path $MODEL_PATH \  # [ModelArguments] Model identifier
         --tune_mm_llm True \                # [TrainingArguments] Train LLM or not
         --tune_mm_vision False \            # [TrainingArguments] Train VIT or not
         --tune_mm_mlp False \               # [TrainingArguments] Train MLP or not
         --dataset_use $DATASETS \           # [DataArguments] Dataset specification
         --output_dir $OUTPUT_DIR \          # Output directory for checkpoints
         --cache_dir $CACHE_DIR \            # [TrainingArguments] Model cache location
         
         # Precision & Memory
         --bf16 \                            # Use bfloat16 precision (Ampere+ GPUs)
         --per_device_train_batch_size 4 \   # Batch size per GPU
         --gradient_accumulation_steps 4 \   # Effective batch size multiplier
         
         # Learning Rate Configuration
         --learning_rate 2e-7 \              # Base learning rate
         --mm_projector_lr 1e-5 \            # [TrainingArguments] Projector-specific LR
         --vision_tower_lr 1e-6 \            # [TrainingArguments] Vision encoder LR
         --optim adamw_torch \               # [TrainingArguments] Optimizer selection
         
         # Sequence Configuration
         --model_max_length 4096 \           # [TrainingArguments] Max sequence length
         --data_flatten True \               # [DataArguments] Concatenate batch sequences
         --data_packing True \               # [DataArguments] Using packing data
         
         # Image Processing
         --max_pixels 576\*28\*28 \               # [DataArguments] Max image pixels (H*W) for image
         --min_pixels 16\*28\*28 \                # [DataArguments] Min image pixels for image
         # Video Processing
         --video_fps 2 \                          # [DataArguments] video fps
         --video_max_frames 8 \                   # [DataArguments] Max frames per video
         --video_min_frames 4 \                   # [DataArguments] Min frames per video
         --video_max_pixels 1664\*28\*28 \        # [DataArguments] Max pixels per video
         --video_min_pixels 256\*28\*28 \         # [DataArguments] Min pixels per video
         
         # Training Schedule
         --num_train_epochs 3 \              # Total training epochs
         --warmup_ratio 0.03 \               # LR warmup proportion
         --lr_scheduler_type "cosine" \      # Learning rate schedule
         --weight_decay 0.01 \               # L2 regularization strength
         
         # Logging & Checkpoints
         --logging_steps 10 \               # Log metrics interval
         --save_steps 500 \                 # Checkpoint save interval
         --save_total_limit 3 \             # Max checkpoints to keep

         # Lora Config
         --lora_enable True \                 # [TrainingArguments] Enable LoRA
         --lora_r 8 \                         # [TrainingArguments] LoRA r
         --lora_alpha 16 \                    # [TrainingArguments] LoRA alpha 
         --lora_dropout 0.0 \                # [TrainingArguments] LoRA dropout

         # Advanced Options
         --deepspeed zero3.json \           # DeepSpeed configuration
```

The script accepts arguments in three categories:

   - Flags to control which components to tune (`tune_mm_vision`, `tune_mm_mlp`, `tune_mm_llm`). If trained with both image and video data, tune_mm_vision should be False: `tune_mm_vision=False`
   - `data_flatten` flag means data in a batch are concat into one sequence
   - `data_packing` requires preprocess with `tools/pack_data.py`
   - Training hyperparameters, the suggested learning rate is from 1e-6 to 2e-7
   - Training resolution is critical for the model performances, hence `--max_pixels` and `--min_pixels` should be properly set
   - Training with Qwen2.5-VL-32B model, you should have 8 80G GPU refering to `scripts/sft_32b.sh`
   - `"_attn_implementation": "flash_attention_2",` could be add in the config.json of the model to use flash attention.
   - The Qwen3VL MoE model does not support DeepSpeed with ZeRO-3. Additionally, Hugging Face’s official implementation does not include support for load balancing loss currently.

13	- `trainer.py`: Main trainer updated from Huggingface Trainer
14	- `train_qwen.py`: Main file for training
15	- `argument.py`: Dataclasses for model, data and training arguments
16	
17	### `data/`
18	- `__init__.py`: Contains datasets configs
19	- `data_processor.py`: Data processing module for QwenVL models
20	- `rope2d.py`: Provide RoPE implementation
21	
22	### `tools`
23	- `process_bbox.ipynb`: Convert bbox into QwenVL format. If you have grounding data, please refer this file to tranform your data.
24	- `pack_data.py`: Pack data into even length buckets.
25	
26	## Requirements
27	
28	You could use follow version of packages:
29	
30	- `torch==2.6.0`
31	- `torchvision==0.21.0`
32	- `transformers==4.57.0.dev0`
33	- `deepspeed==0.17.1`
34	- `flash_attn==2.7.4.post1`
35	- `triton==3.2.0`
36	- `accelerate==1.7.0`
37	- `torchcodec==0.2`
38	- `peft==0.17.1`
39	
40	## Custom Dataset Configuration
41	
42	The customized data should have the format like:
43	
44	### JSON Data Structure
45	
46	**Media Specification**:
47	- `image/video`: Contains path to the media file (required)
48	- Media tags in prompts:
49	    - `<image>` for image understanding tasks
50	    - `<video>` for video understanding tasks
51	- `conversations`: contains the questions and answers
52	
53	### Example Instances:
54	
55	1. **Single Image Example**:
56	```json
57	{
58	    "image": "images/001.jpg",
59	    "conversations": [
60	        {
61	            "from": "human",
62	            "value": "<image>\nWhat's the main object in this picture?"
63	        },
64	        {
65	            "from": "gpt",
66	            "value": "A red apple on a wooden table"
67	        }
68	    ]
69	}
70	```
71	
72	2. **Multi-Image Example**:
73	```json
74	{
75	    "image": ["cats/001.jpg", "cats/002.jpg"],
76	    "conversations": [
77	        {
78	            "from": "human",
79	            "value": "<image>\n<image>\nWhat are the differences between these two cats?"
80	        },
81	        {
82	            "from": "gpt",
83	            "value": "The first cat is an orange tabby with short fur and green eyes, while the second is a gray Siamese with blue eyes and pointed coloration. They also appear to be in different environments - the first is indoors on a couch, the second is outdoors in a garden."
84	        }
85	    ]
86	}
87	```
88	
89	3. **Video Example**:
90	```json
91	{
92	    "video": "videos/005.mp4",
93	    "conversations": [
94	        {
95	            "from": "human",
96	            "value": "<video>\nWhat caused the blue object to move?\nOptions:\n(A) Gravity\n(B) Collision\n(C) Magnetic force"
97	        },
98	        {
99	            "from": "gpt",
100	            "value": "Answer: (B) Collision"
101	        }
102	    ]
103	}
104	```
105	
106	4. **Grounding Example**:
107	```json
108	{
109	    "image": "demo/COCO_train2014_000000580957.jpg",
110	    "conversations": [
111	        {
112	            "from": "human",
113	            "value": "<image>\nLocate house in this image and output the bbox coordinates in JSON format."
114	        },
115	        {
116	            "from": "gpt",
117	            "value": "{\n"bbox_2d": [135, 114, 1016, 672]\n}"
118	        }
119	    ]
120	}
121	```
122	
123	5. **Packed Data Example**:
124	```json
125	[
126	    {
127	        "image": "images/001.jpg",
128	        "conversations": [
129	            {
130	                "from": "human",
131	                "value": "<image>\nWhat's the main object in this picture?"
132	            },
133	            {
134	                "from": "gpt",
135	                "value": "A red apple on a wooden table"
136	            }
137	        ]
138	    },
139	    {
140	        "image": "images/002.jpg",
141	        "conversations": [
142	            {
143	                "from": "human",
144	                "value": "<image>\nWhat's the main object in this picture?"
145	            },
146	            {
147	                "from": "gpt",
148	                "value": "A green orange on a plastic table"
149	            }
150	        ]
151	    }
152	]
153	```
154	
155	Some examples are shown in `demo/single_images.json` and `demo/video.json` and these json files could be used for training.
156	
157	### Dataset config for training
158	
159	To add or modify datasets for training, follow these steps:
160	
161	### Dataset Definition Structure
162	
163	1. **Create a dataset dictionary** in the format in the file `data/__init__.py`:
164	```python
165	DATASET_NAME = {
166	    "annotation_path": "/path/to/annotations.json",
167	    "data_path": "/path/to/image/data",  # Can be empty if paths are in annotations
168	}
169	```
170	
171	2. **Register your dataset** by adding it to the `data_dict`:
172	```python
173	data_dict = {
174	    "your_dataset_name": DATASET_NAME,
175	    # ... other datasets
176	}
177	```
178	
179	### Sampling Rate Control
180	
181	You can optionally specify sampling rates by appending `%X` to the dataset name:
182	- `"dataset_name%50"` will sample 50% of the data
183	- `"dataset_name%20"` will sample 20% of the data
184	
185	### Usage Example
186	
187	1. Define your dataset:
188	```python
189	MY_DATASET = {
190	    "annotation_path": "/data/my_dataset/annotations.json",
191	    "data_path": "/data/my_dataset/images/",
192	}
193	
194	data_dict = {
195	    "my_dataset": MY_DATASET,
196	    "cambrian_737k": CAMBRIAN_737K,  # existing dataset
197	}
198	```
199	
200	2. Use it in training:
201	```python
202	dataset_names = ["my_dataset%50"]  # Will use 50% of your dataset
203	configs = data_list(dataset_names)
204	```
205	
206	### Notes  
207	- The `annotation_path` should point to a JSON or JSONL file containing your dataset annotations.  
208	- The `data_path` can be left empty if the image paths in the annotations are absolute.  
209	- Sampling rates are applied per-dataset when multiple datasets are specified.  
210	- Some datasets you can use directly: `nyu-visionx/Cambrian-10M`, `lmms-lab/LLaVA-NeXT-Data`, `FreedomIntelligence/ALLaVA-4V`, `TIGER-Lab/VisualWebInstruct`.  
211	- The training data should strictly follow this format:  
212	  - One `<image>` tag in the question must correspond to exactly one image file  
213	  - Similarly, `<video>` tags must correspond to video files  
214	  - These special tokens should not appear in the answer text  
215	- For open source data that might have missing images or other issues, you can verify data completeness using `tools/check_image.py`.  
216	
217	
218	## Usage
219	
220	To train a model:
221	
222	```bash
223	#!/bin/bash
224	# Complete QwenVL Training Launch Script with Full Parameter Documentation
225	
226	# ======================
227	# Distributed Configuration
228	# ======================
229	MASTER_ADDR="127.0.0.1"                     # [Required] Master node IP for multi-GPU training
230	MASTER_PORT=$(shuf -i 20000-29999 -n 1)     # Random port to avoid conflicts
231	NPROC_PER_NODE=$(nvidia-smi --list-gpus | wc -l)  # Automatically detects available GPUs
232	
233	# ======================
234	# Path Configuration
235	# ======================
236	MODEL_PATH="/path/to/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct"  # [ModelArguments] Pretrained model path
237	OUTPUT_DIR="./checkpoints"                   # Directory for saving checkpoints
238	CACHE_DIR="./cache"                          # [TrainingArguments] Cache directory for models
239	
240	# ======================
241	# Model Configuration
242	# ======================
243	DATASETS="your_dataset%100"                  # [DataArguments] Dataset with sampling rate
244	
245	# ======================
246	# Training Hyperparameters
247	# ======================
248	torchrun --nproc_per_node=$NPROC_PER_NODE \
249	         --master_addr=$MASTER_ADDR \
250	         --master_port=$MASTER_PORT \
251	         qwenvl/train/train_qwen.py \
252	         # Core Arguments
253	         --model_name_or_path $MODEL_PATH \  # [ModelArguments] Model identifier
254	         --tune_mm_llm True \                # [TrainingArguments] Train LLM or not
255	         --tune_mm_vision False \            # [TrainingArguments] Train VIT or not
256	         --tune_mm_mlp False \               # [TrainingArguments] Train MLP or not
257	         --dataset_use $DATASETS \           # [DataArguments] Dataset specification
258	         --output_dir $OUTPUT_DIR \          # Output directory for checkpoints
259	         --cache_dir $CACHE_DIR \            # [TrainingArguments] Model cache location
260	         
261	         # Precision & Memory
262	         --bf16 \                            # Use bfloat16 precision (Ampere+ GPUs)
263	         --per_device_train_batch_size 4 \   # Batch size per GPU
264	         --gradient_accumulation_steps 4 \   # Effective batch size multiplier
265	         
266	         # Learning Rate Configuration
267	         --learning_rate 2e-7 \              # Base learning rate
268	         --mm_projector_lr 1e-5 \            # [TrainingArguments] Projector-specific LR
269	         --vision_tower_lr 1e-6 \            # [TrainingArguments] Vision encoder LR
270	         --optim adamw_torch \               # [TrainingArguments] Optimizer selection
271	         
272	         # Sequence Configuration
273	         --model_max_length 4096 \           # [TrainingArguments] Max sequence length
274	         --data_flatten True \               # [DataArguments] Concatenate batch sequences
275	         --data_packing True \               # [DataArguments] Using packing data
276	         
277	         # Image Processing
278	         --max_pixels 576\*28\*28 \               # [DataArguments] Max image pixels (H*W) for image
279	         --min_pixels 16\*28\*28 \                # [DataArguments] Min image pixels for image
280	         # Video Processing
281	         --video_fps 2 \                          # [DataArguments] video fps
282	         --video_max_frames 8 \                   # [DataArguments] Max frames per video
283	         --video_min_frames 4 \                   # [DataArguments] Min frames per video
284	         --video_max_pixels 1664\*28\*28 \        # [DataArguments] Max pixels per video
285	         --video_min_pixels 256\*28\*28 \         # [DataArguments] Min pixels per video
286	         
287	         # Training Schedule
288	         --num_train_epochs 3 \              # Total training epochs
289	         --warmup_ratio 0.03 \               # LR warmup proportion
290	         --lr_scheduler_type "cosine" \      # Learning rate schedule
291	         --weight_decay 0.01 \               # L2 regularization strength
292	         
293	         # Logging & Checkpoints
294	         --logging_steps 10 \               # Log metrics interval
295	         --save_steps 500 \                 # Checkpoint save interval
296	         --save_total_limit 3 \             # Max checkpoints to keep
297	
298	         # Lora Config
299	         --lora_enable True \                 # [TrainingArguments] Enable LoRA
300	         --lora_r 8 \                         # [TrainingArguments] LoRA r
301	         --lora_alpha 16 \                    # [TrainingArguments] LoRA alpha 
302	         --lora_dropout 0.0 \                # [TrainingArguments] LoRA dropout
303	
304	         # Advanced Options
305	         --deepspeed zero3.json \           # DeepSpeed configuration
306	```
307	
308	The script accepts arguments in three categories:
309	
310	   - Flags to control which components to tune (`tune_mm_vision`, `tune_mm_mlp`, `tune_mm_llm`). If trained with both image and video data, tune_mm_vision should be False: `tune_mm_vision=False`
311	   - `data_flatten` flag means data in a batch are concat into one sequence
312	   - `data_packing` requires preprocess with `tools/pack_data.py`
313	   - Training hyperparameters, the suggested learning rate is from 1e-6 to 2e-7
314	   - Training resolution is critical for the model performances, hence `--max_pixels` and `--min_pixels` should be properly set
315	   - Training with Qwen2.5-VL-32B model, you should have 8 80G GPU refering to `scripts/sft_32b.sh`
316	   - `"_attn_implementation": "flash_attention_2",` could be add in the config.json of the model to use flash attention.
317	   - The Qwen3VL MoE model does not support DeepSpeed with ZeRO-3. Additionally, Hugging Face’s official implementation does not include support for load balancing loss currently.

import os
import sys
import json
import argparse
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import time
from tqdm import tqdm
from typing import List, Dict, Any
import torch
import warnings
import string
import traceback

# vLLM imports
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from qwen_vl_utils import process_vision_info
from transformers import AutoProcessor

# Local imports from refactored files
from dataset_utils import load_dataset, dump_image, MMMU_preproc
from eval_utils import build_judge, eval_single_sample

# Set vLLM multiprocessing method
os.environ['VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD'] = 'spawn'

def build_mmmu_prompt(line, dump_image_func, dataset):
    """Build MMMU dataset prompt with standard resolution settings."""
    # Standard resolution settings
    MIN_PIXELS = 1280*28*28  # ~1M pixels
    MAX_PIXELS = 5120*28*28  # ~4M pixels
    
    tgt_path = dump_image_func(line)
    question = line['question']
    options = {cand: line[cand] for cand in string.ascii_uppercase if cand in line and not pd.isna(line[cand])}
    options_prompt = 'Options:\n'
    for key, item in options.items():
        options_prompt += f'{key}. {item}\n'
    hint = line['hint'] if ('hint' in line and not pd.isna(line['hint'])) else None
    prompt = ''
    if hint is not None:
        prompt += f'Hint: {hint}\n'
    prompt += f'Question: {question}\n'
    if len(options):
        prompt += options_prompt
        prompt += 'Please select the correct answer from the options above. \n'
    prompt = prompt.rstrip()
    
    # Build messages in standard conversation format
    content = []
    if isinstance(tgt_path, list):
        for p in tgt_path:
            content.append({
                "type": "image",
                "image": p,
                "min_pixels": MIN_PIXELS,
                "max_pixels": MAX_PIXELS
            })
    else:
        content.append({
            "type": "image", 
            "image": tgt_path,
            "min_pixels": MIN_PIXELS,
            "max_pixels": MAX_PIXELS
        })
    content.append({"type": "text", "text": prompt})
    
    # Return messages in standard conversation format
    messages = [{
        "role": "user",
        "content": content
    }]
    
    return messages

def prepare_inputs_for_vllm(messages, processor):
    """
    Prepare inputs for vLLM (following the examples in README.md).
    
    Args:
        messages: List of messages in standard conversation format
        processor: AutoProcessor instance
    
    Returns:
        dict: Input format required by vLLM
    """
    text = processor.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)
    
    # qwen_vl_utils 0.0.14+ required
    image_inputs, video_inputs, video_kwargs = process_vision_info(
        messages,
        image_patch_size=processor.image_processor.patch_size,
        return_video_kwargs=True,
        return_video_metadata=True
    )
    
    mm_data = {}
    if image_inputs is not None:
        mm_data['image'] = image_inputs
    if video_inputs is not None:
        mm_data['video'] = video_inputs
    
    return {
        'prompt': text,
        'multi_modal_data': mm_data,
        'mm_processor_kwargs': video_kwargs
    }

def run_inference(args):
    """Run inference on the MMMU dataset using vLLM."""
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("🚀 MMMU Inference with vLLM (High-Speed Mode)")
    print("="*80 + "\n")
    
    # Load dataset
    data = load_dataset(args.dataset)
    print(f"✓ Loaded {len(data)} samples from {args.dataset}")
    
    # Set up image root directory
    img_root = os.path.join(os.environ['LMUData'], 'images', 'MMMU')

# qwen-vl-utils

Qwen-VL Utils contains a set of helper functions for processing and integrating visual language information with Qwen-VL Series Model.

## Install

```bash
pip install qwen-vl-utils
```

## Usage

### Qwen2VL

```python
from transformers import Qwen2VLForConditionalGeneration, AutoProcessor
from qwen_vl_utils import process_vision_info


# You can directly insert a local file path, a URL, or a base64-encoded image into the position where you want in the text.
messages = [
    # Image
    ## Local file path
    [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "image", "image": "file:///path/to/your/image.jpg"}, {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image."}]}],
    ## Image URL
    [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "image", "image": "http://path/to/your/image.jpg"}, {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image."}]}],
    ## Base64 encoded image
    [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "image", "image": "data:image;base64,/9j/..."}, {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image."}]}],
    ## PIL.Image.Image
    [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "image", "image": pil_image}, {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image."}]}],
    ## Model dynamically adjusts image size, specify dimensions if required.
    [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "image", "image": "file:///path/to/your/image.jpg", "resized_height": 280, "resized_width": 420}, {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image."}]}],
    # Video
    ## Local video path
    [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "video", "video": "file:///path/to/video1.mp4"}, {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this video."}]}],
    ## Local video frames
    [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "video", "video": ["file:///path/to/extracted_frame1.jpg", "file:///path/to/extracted_frame2.jpg", "file:///path/to/extracted_frame3.jpg"],}, {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this video."},],}],
    ## Model dynamically adjusts video nframes, video height and width. specify args if required.
    [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "video", "video": "file:///path/to/video1.mp4", "fps": 2.0, "resized_height": 280, "resized_width": 280}, {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this video."}]}],
]

processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_path)
model = Qwen2VLForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(model_path, torch_dtype="auto", device_map="auto")
text = processor.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)
images, videos = process_vision_info(messages)
inputs = processor(text=text, images=images, videos=videos, padding=True, return_tensors="pt")
print(inputs)
generated_ids = model.generate(**inputs)
print(generated_ids)
```

    ## PIL.Image.Image
    [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "image", "image": pil_image}, {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image."}]}],
    ## Model dynamically adjusts image size, specify dimensions if required.
    [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "image", "image": "file:///path/to/your/image.jpg", "resized_height": 280, "resized_width": 420}, {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image."}]}],

input.rationale: 本仓库是 Qwen3-VL 多模态大模型的官方工程仓库，由四个相对独立的子项目组成：qwen-vl-utils（视觉输入预处理库）、qwen-vl-finetune（SFT 微调框架）、evaluation（基准评测脚手架）与 cookbooks（能力示例笔记本），模型结构代码本身位于 transformers 库中而不在本仓库。因此学习路线设计为：第一单元先让读者从零跑通推理并摸清仓库地图；第二、三单元沿“输入预处理→processor→vLLM 部署”这条所有上层应用共用的调用链推进，其中 qwen-vl-utils 的 smart_resize/帧采样/视频 metadata 是理解 Qwen3-VL 像素预算与时间戳机制的钥匙；第四、五单元进入微调体系，按“数据格式→数据集注册→打包→训练主流程→参数→标签构造→MRoPE 位置编码（rope2d.py 是本仓库中最接近模型内部机制的源码）→拼批 collator→FlashAttention varlen 补丁→LoRA 与分层学习率→DeepSpeed 分布式”的依赖顺序递进拆解源码；第六单元以 mmmu/VideoMME/ODinW-13 三个结构同构的评测目录讲解 run/dataset_utils/eval_utils 三件套模式并实战复现；第七单元面向二次开发，覆盖 cookbooks 能力矩阵、GUI Agent 工具注册（qwen_agent BaseTool 扩展）、2D/3D grounding 坐标体系，最后以“自定义数据集微调端到端闭环”收束全手册。讲义间依赖构成 DAG，先跑通再读码、读完码即实践，每篇均锚定真实源码文件与一个可操作任务。

call_4ced195d99db4bab8e88f52f.head: 96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da
call_4ced195d99db4bab8e88f52f.rationale: 本仓库是 Qwen3-VL 多模态大模型的官方工程仓库，由四个相对独立的子项目组成：qwen-vl-utils（视觉输入预处理库）、qwen-vl-finetune（SFT 微调框架）、evaluation（基准评测脚手架）与 cookbooks（能力示例笔记本），模型结构代码本身位于 transformers 库中而不在本仓库。因此学习路线设计为：第一单元先让读者从零跑通推理并摸清仓库地图；第二、三单元沿“输入预处理→processor→vLLM 部署”这条所有上层应用共用的调用链推进，其中 qwen-vl-utils 的 smart_resize/帧采样/视频 metadata 是理解 Qwen3-VL 像素预算与时间戳机制的钥匙；第四、五单元进入微调体系，按“数据格式→数据集注册→打包→训练主流程→参数→标签构造→MRoPE 位置编码（rope2d.py 是本仓库中最接近模型内部机制的源码）→拼批 collator→FlashAttention varlen 补丁→LoRA 与分层学习率→DeepSpeed 分布式”的依赖顺序递进拆解源码；第六单元以 mmmu/VideoMME/ODinW-13 三个结构同构的评测目录讲解 run/dataset_utils/eval_utils 三件套模式并实战复现；第七单元面向二次开发，覆盖 cookbooks 能力矩阵、GUI Agent 工具注册（qwen_agent BaseTool 扩展）、2D/3D grounding 坐标体系，最后以“自定义数据集微调端到端闭环”收束全手册。讲义间依赖构成 DAG，先跑通再读码、读完码即实践，每篇均锚定真实源码文件与一个可操作任务。

units.title: 单元七：高阶应用与二次开发

data.head: 96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da
data.rationale: 本仓库是 Qwen3-VL 多模态大模型的官方工程仓库，由四个相对独立的子项目组成：qwen-vl-utils（视觉输入预处理库）、qwen-vl-finetune（SFT 微调框架）、evaluation（基准评测脚手架）与 cookbooks（能力示例笔记本），模型结构代码本身位于 transformers 库中而不在本仓库。因此学习路线设计为：第一单元先让读者从零跑通推理并摸清仓库地图；第二、三单元沿“输入预处理→processor→vLLM 部署”这条所有上层应用共用的调用链推进，其中 qwen-vl-utils 的 smart_resize/帧采样/视频 metadata 是理解 Qwen3-VL 像素预算与时间戳机制的钥匙；第四、五单元进入微调体系，按“数据格式→数据集注册→打包→训练主流程→参数→标签构造→MRoPE 位置编码（rope2d.py 是本仓库中最接近模型内部机制的源码）→拼批 collator→FlashAttention varlen 补丁→LoRA 与分层学习率→DeepSpeed 分布式”的依赖顺序递进拆解源码；第六单元以 mmmu/VideoMME/ODinW-13 三个结构同构的评测目录讲解 run/dataset_utils/eval_utils 三件套模式并实战复现；第七单元面向二次开发，覆盖 cookbooks 能力矩阵、GUI Agent 工具注册（qwen_agent BaseTool 扩展）、2D/3D grounding 坐标体系，最后以“自定义数据集微调端到端闭环”收束全手册。讲义间依赖构成 DAG，先跑通再读码、读完码即实践，每篇均锚定真实源码文件与一个可操作任务。

learning_goals: 掌握 messages 内容列表的 image/text/video 三种元素写法
理解 apply_chat_template 到 model.generate 到 batch_decode 的完整调用链
会裁剪 generated_ids 去掉输入部分
lectures.practice_task: 编写一个 infer.py：分别对单图、两张图、一个视频执行推理（统一使用 2B 小模型与 dtype=auto），打印每种的输入 token 数与输出文本。
lectures.title: 第一次推理：单图、多图与视频
lectures.topic: 基于 transformers 的 AutoModelForImageTextToText 与 AutoProcessor 跑通图像、多图、视频三种输入的推理，理解 messages 结构与生成输出裁剪。

learning_goals: 理解 web_demo_mm.py 的参数与双后端设计

会用官方 Docker 镜像一键起服务
lectures.practice_task: 用 --backend hf 启动 web_demo_mm.py 并完成一次上传图片提问；然后阅读 _get_args，写出用 vllm 后端、指定 tensor-parallel-size 为 1 的完整启动命令并记录到笔记。
lectures.title: Web Demo 与 Docker 部署
lectures.topic: 解读 web_demo_mm.py：hf 与 vllm 双后端加载、Gradio 交互流程、流式输出线程，以及官方 Docker 镜像启动方式。

units.title: 单元一：初识 Qwen3-VL 与环境搭建

learning_goals: 理解 process_vision_info 的输入输出契约

理解 return_video_kwargs 与 return_video_metadata 两个开关的作用
lectures.practice_task: 构造包含 1 张图和 1 个视频的 messages，分别以 image_patch_size=14 和 16 调用 process_vision_info，打印两次返回的图像尺寸并解释差异。
lectures.title: qwen-vl-utils 总览与 process_vision_info 主流程
lectures.topic: 从 extract_vision_info 到 process_vision_info 讲清 qwen-vl-utils 的整体数据流，以及 Qwen3-VL 相比 Qwen2.5-VL 新增的 image_patch_size 与 return_video_metadata 机制。

learning_goals: 实现 round/ceil/floor_by_factor 与 smart_resize 的等价逻辑
理解 min_pixels/max_pixels 与视觉 token 数的换算（32 倍空间压缩）
掌握 resized_height/resized_width 精确控制方式
minimal_modules: 像素与 token 预算换算
lectures.practice_task: 对同一张图分别设置 min_pixels=max_pixels=256*32*32、1280*32*32 两档，验证 fetch_image 输出的宽高都是 32 的倍数，并按公式 (H/32)*(W/32) 手算视觉 token 数与实际一致。
lectures.title: 图像链路：fetch_image 与 smart_resize 像素预算
lectures.topic: 精读 fetch_image 与 smart_resize：多种图像来源（本地/URL/base64/PIL）、对齐取整函数、像素预算约束与长宽比保持算法。

learning_goals: 手算给定 fps 与时长下的 nframes
理解 total_pixels 与 max_pixels 联合限制单帧分辨率的逻辑
会用 FORCE_QWENVL_VIDEO_READER 切换解码后端
lectures.practice_task: 下载一个本地 mp4，分别设置 FORCE_QWENVL_VIDEO_READER 为 torchvision/decord/torchcodec（可用则装）调用 fetch_video，记录每次的帧数、分辨率与耗时；再用 fps=1 与 fps=4 各跑一次，验证帧数符合 smart_nframes 公式。
lectures.title: 视频链路：fetch_video、smart_nframes 与三种解码后端
lectures.topic: 精读 fetch_video：smart_nframes 帧数采样公式、torchvision/decord/torchcodec 三种解码后端的选择与回退、total_pixels 总预算对单帧分辨率的约束。

learning_goals: 理解 video_metadata 中各字段的时间语义
解释 Qwen3-VL 用时间戳替代 T-RoPE 绝对时间位置的设计
会用 sample_fps 与帧列表构造带时间信息的视频输入
lectures.practice_task: 调用 fetch_video(ele, return_video_metadata=True, return_video_sample_fps=True)，打印 metadata 的 fps、frames_indices、total_num_frames 字段；再传入 4 帧图片列表 + sample_fps=1，观察合成 metadata 的 total_num_frames 并解释其含义。
lectures.title: video metadata 与 Qwen3-VL 时间戳对齐机制
lectures.topic: 讲解 return_video_metadata 返回的 fps/frames_indices/total_num_frames 如何支撑 Qwen3-VL 的文本-时间戳对齐，以及帧列表输入时的合成 metadata。

units.title: 单元二：多模态输入处理源码（qwen-vl-utils）

learning_goals: 读懂 chat template 渲染后的完整提示串
通过 processor.image_processor.size/video_processor.size 控制视觉 token 预算
掌握 batch 推理的 padding_side 设置
lectures.practice_task: 对同一组 messages 分别执行 tokenize=False 与 tokenize=True，对照观察 <|vision_start|>/<|image_pad|> 等特殊 token；再把 processor.image_processor.size 设为 longest_edge=1280*32*32、shortest_edge=256*32*32，统计 input_ids 长度变化并写入笔记。
lectures.title: 深入 processor：chat template、像素预算与 add_vision_id
lectures.topic: 深入 AutoProcessor 的使用：chat template 渲染、image_processor/video_processor 分离的 size 预算语义、add_vision_id 多图编号与 batch 推理的 padding 细节。

learning_goals: 独立实现 prepare_inputs_for_vllm 函数
理解 prompt/multi_modal_data/mm_processor_kwargs 三个字段的作用
掌握 video 与 video_metadata 的解包与传参
lectures.practice_task: 参照 web_demo_mm.py 与 README 的 vLLM 示例，编写批量离线推理脚本：对 2 张图 + 1 个视频各生成一次结果，正确传入 do_sample_frames 与 video_metadata。
lectures.title: vLLM 离线推理与 prepare_inputs_for_vllm 模式
lectures.topic: 提炼仓库中反复出现的 prepare_inputs_for_vllm 模式：process_vision_info 预处理、multi_modal_data 组装、mm_processor_kwargs 传参与 LLM.generate 离线批量推理。

learning_goals: 掌握 vllm serve 的多模态关键参数
会用 OpenAI SDK 发送 image_url/video_url 请求
通过 extra_body 控制视频采样
lectures.practice_task: 用小模型启动 vllm serve（如 Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct），分别用 OpenAI SDK 发送图像与视频请求；再用 extra_body={"mm_processor_kwargs": {"fps": 4}} 观察视频请求行为变化并记录。
lectures.title: vLLM/SGLang 在线服务部署
lectures.topic: 讲解 vllm serve 与 SGLang 两种在线服务方式的启动参数（tensor-parallel、mm-encoder-tp-mode、media-io-kwargs）以及 OpenAI 风格 API 的图像/视频请求写法。

learning_goals: 写出 1M 上下文的 rope_scaling 配置
解释 Interleaved-MRoPE 下 factor 取 2-3 而非 4 的原因
会启用 flash_attention_2 加速推理
lectures.practice_task: 为一个本地下载的 Qwen3-VL 模型目录编写 1M 上下文的 config.json 修改脚本（max_position_embeddings、rope_scaling、mrope_interleaved），并写出对应的 vllm serve --rope-scaling 启动命令。
lectures.title: 长上下文 YaRN 与 FlashAttention 加速
lectures.topic: 讲解 256K 原生上下文扩展到 1M 的 YaRN 配置：rope_scaling 字段、Interleaved-MRoPE 下 factor 的取值原则，以及 flash_attention_2 的启用方式。

units.title: 单元三：推理进阶与生产部署

learning_goals: 说出 qwenvl 包内各模块职责
理解 tools 目录三个工具的用途
按 README 搭好可训练的依赖版本组合
lectures.practice_task: 按 README 的 Requirements 清单安装 torch/transformers/deepspeed/flash_attn/peft 等依赖并打印各版本；对照目录结构写出 qwenvl 包的模块依赖图。
lectures.title: 微调框架总览：目录、依赖与训练流程
lectures.topic: 介绍 qwen-vl-finetune 的整体结构：train/、data/、tools/、scripts/ 各目录职责，支持的模型代际（Qwen2-VL/2.5-VL/3-VL 及 MoE）与依赖版本要求。

learning_goals: 独立编写符合规范的训练样本 JSON
理解 image/video 字段的单值与列表两种写法
掌握 grounding 样本的 bbox JSON 标注格式
minimal_modules: grounding 样本与 packed 样本
lectures.practice_task: 选 5 张自己的图片各写一句问答，按 single_images.json 的格式制作 my_dataset.json；用 check_image.py（或手写校验脚本）确认所有图片路径可访问、占位符数量与图片数量一致。
lectures.title: 训练数据格式精读：conversations 与 <image>/<video> 占位符
lectures.topic: 精读微调数据格式：image/video 路径字段、human/gpt 对话结构、<image>/<video> 占位符匹配规则，以及 grounding 与 packed 数据示例。

learning_goals: 理解 annotation_path 与 data_path 的分工
实现自定义数据集注册
掌握 %X 采样率语法
lectures.practice_task: 在 data/__init__.py 中注册 MY_DATASET（指向上一讲制作的 my_dataset.json），运行 data_list(["my_dataset%50"]) 验证 sampling_rate 解析，再实例化 LazySupervisedDataset 观察打印的样本总数。
lectures.title: 数据集注册表与采样率控制
lectures.topic: 讲解 qwenvl/data/__init__.py 的数据集注册机制：data_dict 字典、dataset_use 解析、%X 百分比采样率，以及 LazySupervisedDataset 如何读取 JSON/JSONL 标注。

learning_goals: 理解按 token 长度装箱的 packing 策略
掌握 pre-calculate 长度对训练效率的意义
会为自有数据生成 packed 标注
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 pack_data.py 的装箱主流程后，写一个 50 行以内的简化打包器：估算每条样本 token 数，用 binpacking 把 my_dataset.json 打包成不超过 8192 token 的桶，输出 packed json 并抽查一个桶内的样本顺序。
lectures.title: 数据打包 pack_data.py 与长度分桶
lectures.topic: 解读 tools/pack_data.py：用处理器预估每条样本 token 长度、按目标长度 binpacking 装箱生成 packed 标注，以及 check_image.py 的数据完整性校验。

units.title: 单元四：微调数据准备

learning_goals: 跟踪 train() 从参数解析到 trainer.train() 的完整流程
理解 set_model 三个开关控制的模块范围
掌握断点续训与 processor 保存逻辑
lectures.practice_task: 画出 train_qwen.py 的调用流程图（模型加载→tokenizer→LoRA/冻结→data_module→Trainer→保存）；用 Qwen3-VL-2B + demo 数据以 num_train_epochs=0.01 启动一次冒烟训练，确认 loss 正常反传。
lectures.title: train_qwen.py 训练主流程精读
lectures.topic: 逐段精读训练入口：按模型名自动选择 Qwen2VL/Qwen2.5VL/Qwen3VL/Qwen3VLMoe 类、set_model 冻结策略、梯度检查点、断点续训与保存流程。

learning_goals: 按 dataclass 归类脚本中的每个参数
理解视频相关八个数据参数的联动关系
独立改写出适配自己场景的启动脚本
lectures.practice_task: 对照 scripts/sft_qwen3_4b.sh，把其中每个参数标注归属（模型/数据/训练三类）并解释含义；复制出一份单卡 2B 模型的启动脚本，调整 batch_size、model_max_length、max_pixels 并注释理由。
lectures.title: 参数体系：argument.py 三组 dataclass 与脚本对照
lectures.topic: 精读 ModelArguments/DataArguments/TrainingArguments 三组 dataclass，并与 sft_qwen3_4b.sh 中的命令行参数逐条对照。

learning_goals: 跟踪 <image> 占位符到 messages content 的转换过程
理解 77091/151645 两个魔法数字与标签区间的对应
掌握 update_processor_pixels 的预算注入方式
lectures.practice_task: 在 __getitem__ 处单步调试一条 demo 样本，打印 input_ids、labels 和 pixel_values 形状；用 tokenizer.decode 分别解码 labels 中非 -100 的区间，验证恰好是 assistant 回复（含结束符）。
lectures.title: LazySupervisedDataset 与标签掩码构造
lectures.topic: 精读 data_processor.py 的样本处理：_build_messages 的占位符替换、preprocess_qwen_visual 中基于 token id 的 assistant 区间标签掩码、__getitem__ 的容错重试。

learning_goals: 解释 position_ids 三行分别编码什么维度
对比三代实现的 t_index 差异（绝对时间/时间戳/帧序号）
理解 text 段与 vision 段位置 id 的衔接规则
lectures.practice_task: 构造一条含 1 张图（grid_thw=[1,64,64]）和若干文本 token 的 input_ids，分别调用三个 get_rope_index_* 打印 3×L 的 position_ids；标出视觉段的 t/h/w 三行取值，并用文字说明 Qwen3-VL 中 t_index 恒为 0 的原因。
lectures.title: rope2d.py：三代 MRoPE 位置编码与 Interleaved-MRoPE
lectures.topic: 精读 rope2d.py 中 get_rope_index_2/25/3 三个实现，对比 Qwen2-VL、Qwen2.5-VL（T-RoPE 时间步进）与 Qwen3-VL（时间戳编码、t_index 恒 0）的位置 id 计算差异。

learning_goals: 理解常规 collator 的 pad 与 grid 拼接
解释 Flattened collator 中 attention_mask 变为累计序列长度的设计
区分 data_flatten 与 data_packing 两个开关
lectures.practice_task: 构造 2 条短样本分别过两种 collator，打印 input_ids/labels/position_ids/attention_mask 的形状与内容；重点验证 Flattened 版本输出的 attention_mask 是首元素为 0 的累计长度向量（如 [0, 12, 12+35]）。
lectures.title: 两种 DataCollator：常规 padding 与 flatten/packing 拼接
lectures.topic: 对比 DataCollatorForSupervisedDataset 与 FlattenedDataCollatorForSupervisedDataset：前者按 batch padding，后者把多样本拼成一条序列并用 cumsum 序列长度充当 attention_mask。

learning_goals: 理解 varlen 注意力对拼接训练的必要性
解释 cu_seqlens 的构造与 causal 语义
掌握跨四类模型模块的运行时替换手法
lectures.practice_task: 为 flash_attention_forward 与 replace_qwen2_vl_attention_class 写逐行中文注释，说明 cu_seqlens 如何由上一讲的 collator 生成、max_seqlen 如何计算；再用一段伪代码演示若不替换会发生样本间注意力泄漏。
lectures.title: trainer.py：FlashAttention varlen 替换与 monkey patch
lectures.topic: 精读 trainer.py：flash_attn_varlen_func 按 cu_seqlens 分段做因果注意力、qwen2vl/qwen3vl 两套 forward 替换、create_causal_mask 短路，以及 create_optimizer 的多参数组改造。

learning_goals: 配置 q/k/v/o_proj 的 LoRA 训练
理解 vision/merger/LLM 三模块独立解冻粒度
实现 mm_projector_lr 与 vision_tower_lr 分组
lectures.practice_task: 用 sft_30a3b_lora.sh 的参数在 2B 模型 + demo 数据上跑一次 LoRA 微调（lora_r=8, lora_alpha=16），训练后用 peft 合并权重并对比合并前后对同一张图的输出。
lectures.title: LoRA 微调与分层学习率
lectures.topic: 讲解 train_qwen.py 中的 LoRA 分支（target_modules 为 q/k/v/o_proj）与 trainer.py 中按 merger/visual 名称划分的 mm_projector_lr、vision_tower_lr 多参数组优化器。

learning_goals: 区分 ZeRO-2/3/offload 的显存与通信取舍
按模型规模选择对应脚本模板
理解 MoE 模型不支持 ZeRO-3 的限制
lectures.practice_task: 对比 zero2.json/zero3.json/zero3_offload.json 的字段差异并写成对照表；根据本机 GPU 数量与显存选择一档配置，说明单卡 24G 跑 2B 模型时应选哪档及理由。
lectures.title: DeepSpeed 配置与多规格训练脚本
lectures.topic: 对比 zero2/zero3/zero3_offload 三份 DeepSpeed 配置与 4B/30B-A3B/32B 等不同规格的 sft 脚本，理解显存、并行与 offload 的取舍及 MoE 模型的 ZeRO-3 限制。

units.title: 单元五：微调核心源码

跟踪从数据集加载到判分的数据流
理解 OpenAIWrapper 兜底判分的设计
lectures.practice_task: 以 mmmu 目录为例画出从 load_dataset→build_mmmu_prompt→prepare_inputs_for_vllm→llm.generate→build_judge→eval_single_sample 的数据流图，并标注每个环节所在的文件与函数。

learning_goals: 理解多选题 prompt 的组装规则
掌握按数据集设定 min/max_pixels 的技巧
跑通一次完整 MMMU 评测并读数

lectures.title: MMMU 图文混评基准实战
lectures.topic: 以 MMMU 为例实战：build_mmmu_prompt 的题目/选项拼接与 MIN/MAX_PIXELS 分辨率设定、vLLM 批量推理循环与准确率统计。

learning_goals: 区分 Instruct 与 Thinking 模式的采样超参
看懂 infer/eval 两段式脚本设计
跑通一次视频理解评测
minimal_modules: 推理与评测两段式脚本

learning_goals: 理解 bbox JSON 输出格式的解析规则
掌握相对/绝对坐标的归一化处理
